evidence.audit_scope: Section 12 Micro Benchmarks reusable C++ comparison-language programs; checked for continued semantic validity under the current C++ toolchain/capability contract. No measurements were taken or reused; this is a source/harness currency review only.
evidence.conclusion: The C++ micro-benchmark source/harness (mb00.cpp-mb11.cpp) remains semantically valid against the current C++ toolchain/capability contract (GCC and Clang releases current as of Sept 2026). No measurements were reused from prior runs; this audit is a static/documentary review only.
language_level_findings: All 12 files use only standard C++17 constructs (structured bindings in mb11.cpp, std::string_view and integer-overload std::from_chars in mb10.cpp, std::chrono::steady_clock, <charconv>). No C++20/23-only syntax is used.

Current mainstream toolchains still compile this code without modification: GCC 11 through GCC 15 default to -std=gnu++17, and GCC 16 defaults to C++20; Clang 16 and later default to the GNU++17 dialect. Both defaults, and any explicit -std=c++17/20/23 pin, compile every file unchanged.

No language feature used by these files was removed or altered in a source-breaking way between C++17 and C++20/23 (the C++20 removals/deprecations found in research -- volatile-qualified structured bindings, auto_ptr, register, comma-in-subscript -- do not appear in any mb0x.cpp file).

std::from_chars for integer types (the only from_chars usage present, in mb10.cpp) has been available in libstdc++ since GCC 8 and is standard in current libc++/libstdc++/MSVC STL; the floating-point from_chars gap that existed in older libstdc++/libc++ releases is not exercised by this code, so no fragility remains there.

The mb10.cpp buffered-I/O idiom (rdbuf()->pubsetbuf(buf, size) called before open()) matches the documented libstdc++ manual example pattern and is the portable, standard-conformant ordering; this technique remains valid across current standard library implementations.

All Lehmer/MINSTD LCG parameters (multiplier 48271, modulus 2147483647) and fixed seeds are byte-identical across mb01-mb11, preserving the frozen algorithm/input-data/workload-size contract required by Section 12 for cross-language comparability.

Every mb01-mb11 file implements the required 'once'/'steady' program-mode switch with a K-iteration steady loop, per-iteration ITER timing line with immediate flush, and a volatile anti-elimination sink/mutation, consistently applied across the whole family so no workload can be silently optimized away by the compiler.
mb00.cpp remains the minimal ordinary program (prints HELLO, exits 0) required as the MB-00 baseline for Runtime Overhead and Startup Latency measurement.
No GPU acceleration, hand-written SIMD, or externally optimized native library is used in any file, consistent with the Language Quality fairness rules for reusable comparison-language programs.

No unused-toolchain-only or platform-specific extensions were found; all files rely only on the ISO C++ standard library headers (<cstdio>, <chrono>, <vector>, <unordered_map>, <unordered_set>, <fstream>, <charconv>, <cmath>, <string>, <string_view>), which remain fully supported by current GCC/Clang/libstdc++/libc++.
residual_recommendations: Pin an explicit -std=c++17 (or higher) flag in the build harness for reproducibility, even though current compiler defaults already satisfy the code's requirements, so a future compiler default change cannot silently alter behavior.
No source changes are required at this time; the artifact remains reusable as-is.
